decisions.statement: Every supervisor's files are under the user's runtime directory.
A supervisor's own folder is named for the id of its agent.
No file a supervisor writes while running is inside the checkout.
A file here goes when the user logs out rather than outliving the machine.
What outlives a run is the day of lines filed beside a page.
A path the kernel binds a socket at is at most 107 bytes.
The user's runtime directory is emptied when that user logs out.
The socket the OAuth proxy is reached on is in the user's runtime directory.
That socket is named for its agent rather than held in a folder of its own.
A file too big to name a socket has a runtime folder of that agent's own.
No such folder is the directory the sockets themselves sit in.
The runtime directory is worked out from the user rather than read from the environment.
A caller may name another base folder.
A test working apart from the real folder names another base folder.
Nothing here makes a folder or opens a file.

definition: where a supervisor's own files are while that supervisor runs
